teaser.text: Allstate is an insurer: it takes premiums in exchange for promises to help customers recover from specified losses. Its central business is personal auto and home coverage, but the company also sells other protections and services through several routes to market.

stock.title: Allstate stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Allstate's stock forecast weighs bear, base and bull scenarios against underwriting, catastrophe risk, cash generation and valuation.
stock.opening: Allstate's weighted path reaches $264.54 in October 2027, $292.28 in October 2028 and $326.62 in October 2029. It hinges on profitable underwriting surviving catastrophe costs, reserve changes and softer pricing.
stock.closing: The full memo explains Allstate's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Allstate's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: Allstate’s weighted path reaches $264.54 in October 2027, $292.28 in October 2028 and $326.62 in October 2029. These prices imply total returns of 8%, 21% and 37% with dividends. The final-date range is much wider: $106.29 in the bear case to $623.61 in the bull case, against today’s $247.88.

The forecast assigns 30% to the bear case, 50% to the base case and 20% to the bull case. The central path offers attractive upside, but the possible loss remains large because Allstate’s earnings have moved sharply with underwriting conditions.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Allstate?

paragraphs.text: The bear case uses $8,400 million, $7,500 million and $6,700 million as injury severity, catastrophes and weaker investment support overwhelm premium growth. The bull case uses $10,800 million, $11,880 million and $13,068 million if applications become persistent policies, severity stabilizes and reinsurance limits severe-event damage. The $1,650 million Q3 catastrophe estimate shows why catastrophe costs remain inside the forecast.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Allstate really make and give back?

paragraphs.text: A reserve is not cash in a separate account. It is an estimate of the eventual cost of claims, including claims not yet reported. As repair bills, medical evidence or lawsuits develop, the estimate can rise or fall, changing current profit before the related cash is paid. Allstate reported $10,110 million of operating cash flow in 2025, but reserve and premium-related movements make that cash flow unlike a retailer’s cash profit.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Allstate today?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, compares a share price with earnings per share. In the second quarter of 2026, Allstate reported $3.2 billion of net income but $2.3 billion of adjusted net income. The difference mainly reflected gains from higher public-equity valuations, which can reverse without adding insurance customers or cash from policyholders. The useful question is therefore whether the low P/E reflects durable underwriting profit or a temporarily enlarged denominator.

dividend.title: Allstate dividend: payout and cash coverage
dividend.meta_description: Allstate dividend history, current payout, cash-flow context, yield, and the risks that could change future dividends.
dividend.opening: Allstate pays $1.08 per share quarterly, or $4.32 annually in the forecast. Its 2025 operating cash flow was $10,110 million, but conventional free cash flow is a weak shortcut for an insurer, so dividend coverage depends on claims, reserves, capital and reinsurance.
dividend.closing: The full memo also answers questions about Allstate’s business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Allstate pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends start at $4.32 per share in every case for October 2027 because the current $1.08 quarterly rate supplies four payments. The base case grows that amount 5% annually to $4.54 and $4.77. The bull case repeats the latest 8% increase, reaching $4.67 and $5.04. The bear case holds at $4.32 because claims pressure could preserve capital, despite increases from $3.24 in 2021 to $4.00 in 2025.

blocks.heading: Does Allstate’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: A reserve is not cash in a separate account. It is an estimate of the eventual cost of claims, including claims not yet reported. As repair bills, medical evidence or lawsuits develop, the estimate can rise or fall, changing current profit before the related cash is paid. Allstate reported $10,110 million of operating cash flow in 2025, but reserve and premium-related movements make that cash flow unlike a retailer’s cash profit.

Conventional free cash flow is also a weak shortcut because premiums arrive before many claims are paid. The better test is whether Allstate can maintain profitable underwriting, absorb a severe catastrophe year and return capital while preserving statutory reserves and reinsurance protection. That is what the stock’s valuation is really asking investors to believe.

blocks.heading: What has Allstate guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Allstate can reach $326.62 by October 2029 if underwriting strength persists as catastrophe costs and earnings normalize. Management aims to grow personal insurance through broader distribution and improved affordability while keeping underwriting profitable. It authorized up to $4.00 billion in common-share repurchases from February 2026 to February 2028, but that ceiling is not a spending commitment.

Management’s broader promise is to grow personal insurance by widening distribution and improving affordability while keeping underwriting profitable. It has not provided, in the guidance identified here, a specific earnings or policy-growth forecast. That makes the next question whether operating results can justify using the capital.

blocks.heading: What has Allstate's recent revenue and profit trend shown?

paragraphs.text: Q2 2026 was a strong quarter for underwriting, but its net income was not a clean recurring earnings rate.

Reported underwriting improved substantially, while the underlying result was nearly flat year over year. Lower catastrophe losses and favorable prior-year reserve revisions helped the reported figure, so the underlying measure is the better test of current performance.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Allstate's next results?

paragraphs.text: The Q3 report is the key checkpoint because it will translate the catastrophe estimate into reported results. Investors should look for changes in claims, reserves, policy counts, premiums, and underwriting profit.
